questions.prompt: State Clean Architecture's single dependency rule as this guide gives it. Then, for Domain, Application, Infrastructure and Web, say what each layer must not own (and, for Application, the critical thing it does own), including the one-question test for an Infrastructure file and the evidence that Web's endpoints hold no business decisions.

keyPoints.text: Source-code dependencies point inward, toward policy and away from mechanism.
keyPoints.quote: source-code dependencies point *inward*, toward policy, away from mechanism.

keyPoints.text: Domain must not own persistence knowledge, anything HTTP, or use-case orchestration.
keyPoints.quote: Must not own: persistence knowledge, HTTP anything, use-case orchestration.

keyPoints.text: Application owns the interfaces that the outer layers must implement.
keyPoints.quote: the interfaces outer layers must implement

keyPoints.text: Application must not own how identity is stored, which database runs, or HTTP status codes.
keyPoints.quote: Must not own: how identity is stored, which database runs, HTTP status codes.

keyPoints.text: Infrastructure test: you can describe any of its files' jobs without naming a business concept.
keyPoints.quote: could you describe any Infrastructure file's job without mentioning a business concept?

keyPoints.text: Web owns HTTP translation but must not own business decisions.
keyPoints.quote: Must not own: business decisions.

keyPoints.text: The proof: the fattest endpoint logic in the repo is an id-consistency check.
keyPoints.quote: the fattest endpoint logic in the repo is an id-consistency check

questions.prompt: Explain the guide's three specimens of boundaries done well: where IUser is defined and implemented and what that buys (now and for a future transport), how IIdentityService keeps ASP.NET Identity out of Application, and how domain events travel between layers without any wrong-direction reference.

keyPoints.text: IUser is a two-property interface defined inward in Application.
CurrentUser in Web implements it from HttpContext, outward.
keyPoints.quote: implements it from `HttpContext` outward.

keyPoints.text: Tests can swap it for a mock trivially.
keyPoints.quote: tests swap it with a mock trivially

keyPoints.text: A future message-queue consumer could implement it from message metadata.
keyPoints.quote: a future message-queue consumer could implement it from message metadata.

keyPoints.text: Application asks role and policy questions through IIdentityService without knowing ASP.NET Identity exists.
keyPoints.quote: without knowing ASP.NET Identity exists.

keyPoints.text: All the UserManager and ClaimsPrincipal machinery stays in Infrastructure's IdentityService.
keyPoints.quote: All `UserManager`/`ClaimsPrincipal` machinery stays in

keyPoints.text: Domain announces an event, Application reacts in a handler, and an Infrastructure SaveChanges interceptor carries it.
No layer references the wrong direction.
keyPoints.quote: No layer references the wrong direction.

questions.prompt: Walk through the boundary leaks the guide catalogs: why the Users endpoint and Program.cs reaching into Infrastructure are tolerated, how you should describe EF Core types in Application contracts, and what binding HTTP JSON straight to command records trades and when it starts to cost. Then give the transferable procedure for finding layer violations in any repo.

keyPoints.text: The Users endpoint takes Identity types directly because wrapping MapIdentityApi in CQRS would be ceremony; know it is an exception.
keyPoints.quote: wrapping `MapIdentityApi` in CQRS would be ceremony

keyPoints.text: Program.cs may import Infrastructure because the composition root is allowed to know everything.
keyPoints.quote: composition root is *allowed* to know everything

keyPoints.text: DbSet in IApplicationDbContext is deliberate and ADR'd: call it a documented tradeoff, not a violation.
keyPoints.quote: Say "documented tradeoff," not "violation"

keyPoints.text: Binding transport DTOs straight to commands trades an anti-corruption seam for less mapping code.
keyPoints.quote: binding transport DTOs directly to application commands trades an anti-corruption seam for less mapping code

keyPoints.text: It costs the day an HTTP field should not reach the handler, such as a server-set OwnerId.
keyPoints.quote: the cost appears the day one HTTP field shouldn't reach the handler

keyPoints.text: Read the project references first, because the dependency graph cannot lie.
keyPoints.quote: references first — the dependency graph can't lie.

keyPoints.text: Grep inner layers for outer namespaces, and treat framework types in interface signatures as coupling decisions.
keyPoints.quote: Grep inner layers for outer namespaces

keyPoints.text: Check where HttpContext appears; if it shows up in Application, the boundary is gone.
keyPoints.quote: If it shows up in Application, the boundary is gone.
